questions.question: What is the correct terminology for melted rock depending on its location?
options: It is called magma on Earth's surface and lava underground.
It is called lava on Earth's surface and magma underground.
It is called magma in both locations.
It is called lava in both locations.

questions.question: What is the main difference in formation location between extrusive and intrusive igneous rocks?
options: Extrusive igneous rock forms inside the crust, while intrusive forms outside Earth's crust.
Extrusive igneous rock forms outside Earth's crust, while intrusive forms inside the crust.
Extrusive igneous rock forms in the mantle, while intrusive forms in the core.
Extrusive igneous rock forms in water, while intrusive forms on dry land.

questions.question: What primary factor determines the size of the crystals that form in a cooling igneous rock?
options: The rate at which the melted rock cools.
The total volume of melted rock present.
The depth at which the rock is buried after cooling.
The atmospheric pressure above the rock.

questions.question: How are the atoms arranged inside any crystal structure?
options: In random, constantly shifting positions.
In small, isolated clumps with no repeating structure.
In a very regular, repeating pattern.
In concentric circular layers that do not touch.

questions.question: Under what conditions do metamorphic rocks form, leading to the alteration of their original structures?
options: Rapid cooling at Earth's surface in the presence of water.
Extreme pressure and temperature deep underground.
Slow evaporation of mineral-rich water at room temperature.
Low pressure and freezing temperatures in glacial areas.

questions.question: What is the scientific definition of a mineral?
options: A man-made mixture of different organic materials.
A naturally occurring pure substance with a crystal structure.
Any rock that contains visible fossils of ancient organisms.
A liquid fuel source extracted from deep within Earth's crust.

questions.question: What is the name of the dense rocky layer located directly beneath Earth's crust?
options: The inner core.
The atmosphere.
The outer core.
The mantle.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the structure of Earth's core?
options: A liquid inner core surrounded by a solid metallic outer core.
A completely gaseous core made of hydrogen and helium.
A solid metallic core surrounded by a liquid outer core.
A hollow core containing dense volcanic gases.

questions.question: What scientific evidence supports the idea that Earth's continents were once joined together in a single landmass?
options: Matching rock formations and fossils found across different continents.
The identical temperature of the oceans surrounding each continent.
Historical written records from early human civilizations.
The uniform depth of the crust under all the continents.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding Earth's tectonic plates?
options: They are large, unbroken solid shells that never move.
They are pieces of the crust that move very, very slowly.
They are rapidly spinning metallic plates in the outer core.
They are soft, muddy layers directly beneath the oceans.

questions.question: Which feature is characteristic of the structure of sedimentary rocks?
options: They consist of large, aligned crystals that grew from magma.
They are made of liquid metal layers that cooled slowly.
They contain distinct grains that are stuck together.
They are completely uniform with no visible grains or particles.

questions.question: How do the crystal arrangements of igneous and metamorphic rocks typically differ?
options: Igneous crystals mostly line up, while metamorphic crystals point in many directions.
Igneous crystals point in many directions, while metamorphic crystals mostly line up.
Igneous rocks have no crystals, while metamorphic rocks are made entirely of large crystals.
Both rock types have crystals that are perfectly aligned in parallel rows.

questions.question: What determines whether a rock is porous or non-porous?
options: Rocks with interlocking grains or crystals are non-porous; those without are porous.
Rocks with interlocking grains or crystals are porous; those without are non-porous.
Rocks containing fossils are always non-porous; all other rocks are porous.
Rocks formed underwater are non-porous; rocks formed on land are porous.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the melting point of rock?
options: It is very low, allowing rocks to melt easily at room temperature.
It is very high, requiring extreme heat for rocks to melt.
It is exactly the same as the boiling point of water.
It depends only on the amount of light shining on the rock.

questions.question: Why are the aligned crystals in some metamorphic rocks useful for practical applications?
options: They allow the rocks to dissolve very quickly in rainwater.
They make the rocks highly elastic so they can bend like rubber.
They give them properties like being easily separated into flat sheets.
They cause the rocks to glow brightly in the dark.

questions.question: What geological condition between tectonic plates allows large crystals to grow inside solid rock?
options: High pressure and temperature.
Extremely rapid cooling by ocean currents.
Intense exposure to ultraviolet solar radiation.
Complete absence of gravitational forces.
